summary: Iteration 162 - iPad/Tablet Login Fix Testing. The fix for iOS/iPad autofill partially works. 3/4 test scenarios pass. One edge case fails: when email field has autoFocus and values are set via pure DOM manipulation (no events), clicking submit triggers blur which clears the email value before FormData can read it.

ui_bugs.issue: When email input has autoFocus and values are set via pure DOM manipulation (simulating worst-case iOS autofill), clicking submit button triggers onBlur which causes React re-render, resetting email value to empty state before handleLogin can read FormData
ui_bugs.root_cause: React controlled component behavior: onBlur triggers re-render, value prop (empty state) overwrites DOM value
reproduction_steps: 2. Set email/password values via pure DOM manipulation (no events)
4. Blur event fires on email field
5. React re-renders, email value reset to empty state
7. Login fails silently (no error shown because email is empty)
ui_bugs.workaround: If user clicks elsewhere first (blurring email field) before autofill, then clicks submit, login works

tests: POST /api/auth/login with admin@bidblitz.ae / BidBlitz2026! - PASS (200 OK)
TEST 2: Autofill with input events - PASS

normal_typing_login.details: Normal typing login on iPad viewport (768x1024) works correctly with admin@bidblitz.ae / BidBlitz2026!

autofill_with_events.details: When autofill dispatches input events, the onInput handler updates React state and login works

dom_manipulation_email_not_focused.details: When email field is NOT focused (user clicked elsewhere first), pure DOM manipulation + submit works

dom_manipulation_email_focused.details: When email field HAS focus (autoFocus), pure DOM manipulation + submit fails because blur clears value

action_items: FIX REQUIRED: Modify AuthPage.jsx to handle the edge case where email field has focus and values are set without events
SUGGESTED FIX 1: In handleLogin, read DOM values BEFORE any blur can trigger (use mousedown instead of click, or capture phase)
SUGGESTED FIX 2: Remove autoFocus from email field, or add onBlur handler that preserves DOM value if state is empty
SUGGESTED FIX 3: Use uncontrolled inputs with refs instead of controlled components for login form
SUGGESTED FIX 4: In onBlur handler, check if DOM value differs from state and update state before re-render
critical_code_review_comments: The fix correctly added onInput handler and FormData extraction in handleLogin
However, the fix doesn't account for React's controlled component behavior during blur
When email field has autoFocus and user clicks submit, blur fires BEFORE submit handler
During blur, React re-renders and resets DOM value to empty state value
By the time handleLogin runs, FormData already contains empty email
The inputRef.current?.value fallback also returns empty because DOM was already reset
seed_data_creation: None - used existing seeded admin account
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 162 found a specific edge case bug in the iPad autofill fix. The fix works for most scenarios (normal typing, autofill with events, DOM manipulation when email not focused). But fails when: (1) email field has autoFocus, (2) values set via pure DOM manipulation (no events), (3) user clicks submit. The blur event on email field triggers React re-render which resets email value to empty state before FormData can read it. Main agent needs to fix this edge case.

mocked_apis.note: All endpoints use real backend with MongoDB

rca_of_the_issue.root_cause: React controlled component behavior conflicts with iOS autofill edge case
technical_details: Email input has autoFocus, so it starts focused on page load
iOS autofill may set values via pure DOM manipulation without dispatching events
When user clicks submit button, email field loses focus (blur event)
onBlur handler calls setFocused(false), triggering React re-render
During re-render, React sees value prop is empty (state is empty) and resets DOM value
By the time handleLogin runs, both FormData and inputRef.current.value are empty
Login fails silently because email is empty
rca_of_the_issue.affected_scenarios: Only affects worst-case iOS autofill where no events are dispatched AND email field has focus
rca_of_the_issue.mitigation: User can work around by clicking elsewhere first (blurring email) before autofill, then clicking submit
